payload.ambiguity_note: Using only the provided train and validation metadata, the main ambiguity risks are patch-level label ambiguity and visual overlap among histology classes at 28x28 RGB resolution. The class counts and proportions are nearly identical between train and validation, and the imbalance ratio is modest, so there is no strong evidence of split-level distribution mismatch from these statistics alone. However, several labels are likely to be visually confusable in small tissue patches: background, debris, and mucus can appear as low-structure or amorphous regions; adipose may resemble background or empty space depending on staining and cropping; smooth muscle and cancer-associated stroma can share fibrous or spindle-cell texture; normal colon mucosa and colorectal adenocarcinoma epithelium may overlap when a patch contains mixed glandular architecture; and lymphocytes may be confused with small debris or nuclear fragments. Because the images are intentionally small, boundary effects, mixed-tissue patches, and annotation uncertainty are plausible ambiguity sources. The held-out test split is locked and unavailable, so these risks cannot be validated against test performance.
